Synopsis:
The players have agreed to help the Harpers ambush a caravan of Absolute cultists and prisoners. You've just arrived at the ambush site - the mood is tense, words are spoken in harsh whispers. When the Caravan arrives there's a monsterous drider at its head, muttering to itself, talking to an imaginary queen/majesty that represents the voice of his God, The Absolute. The player can try to trick the drider into handing over its magic lantern (the Moonlantern - a glowing lantern hanging from the end of a staff), although that could leave the drider exposed to the worst effects of the curse. Will likely end in combat, either because you signaled the Harpers to spring their ambush or because the drider got suspicious and attacked.

Cluster Contexts:
- SCL_Drider_HarpersAndPlayersAmbush.json: You and your party have joined the Harpers to ambush an Absolute cultist caravan escorting prisoners; everyone is hidden and the mood is tense as the caravan arrives. A monstrous drider leads the column, muttering to an imagined “queen/majesty” (the voice of the Absolute) and carrying a glowing Moonlantern on a staff — a magical item tied to the drider’s curse. The drider is known from an earlier Moonrise Tower encounter, and cultists around it show a mix of ecstatic devotion and contempt from other guards; nearby sentries are primed to be suspicious and quick to escalate. Trying to trick or remove the Moonlantern might cure or disastrously expose the drider to the curse, and the scene will likely end in combat whether you trigger the Harpers or the drider becomes suspicious.
- SCL_Drider_PlayersAmbush.json: You and the Harpers have set an ambush for a caravan of Absolute cultists escorting prisoners; you've just arrived at the staked‑out site and the mood is tense and whisper‑quiet. A drider leads the caravan and compulsively speaks to an imagined “majesty” — the Absolute — often projecting that voice through telepathic mind‑melds that can reveal “True Souls.” Fanatical cultists like Kar’niss treat the drider as their mouthpiece and guard its Moonlantern (a glowing lantern hung from a staff), while other sentries may sneer with contempt. The player can try to trick the drider into giving up the Moonlantern, but that risks exposing the drider to the curse and will very likely end in combat — either when the Harpers spring the ambush or if the drider and guards grow suspicious; note that routine telepathic checks here will likely register any tadpole and trigger orders to report to Disciple Z’rell.
- SCL_Drider_CaravanAmbushed.json: Harpers ambush the caravan and the players. If this dialog succeeds on starting, the players can decide to fight the Harpers or change sides and help the ambushers fight the drider.
- SCL_Drider_HarpersAtInn.json: The players encounter a squad of Harpers at the Last Light Inn who're preparing to set out on a dangerous mission to ambush a drider and some cultists in the shadow-cursed lands. Lassandra, a Harper scout that the player may have helped previously, might be there.
- SCL_Drider_HarperRanger_000_AfterAmbush.json: Harper Ranger after the fight with the Drider. You may or may not have started the fight on his side. After the ambush has ended, a prisoner threatens you, telling you to hand over the lantern.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Kar'niss: We bring more to your church every day, my Queen. Your followers are legion. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: The Drider appears, leading a caravan of Absolute Cultists and prisoners, Moonlantern in his hand. The Caravan is silent, bar the drider muttering quietly to itself.NodeContext: Drider muttering to himself (node 40)

context: You and the Harpers have staked out an ambush for a caravan of Absolute cultists who are escorting prisoners; everyone is hidden and the mood is tense and whisper‑quiet as the column arrives. A monstrous drider leads the caravan, compulsively muttering to an imagined “majesty” (the voice of the Absolute) and bearing a glowing Moonlantern on a staff — a magical object tied to the drider’s curse and remembered from an earlier Moonrise Tower encounter. Cultists around it range from ecstatic devotees (e.g., Kar’niss) to sneering guards, and nearby sentries are primed to be suspicious and escalate quickly. You can attempt to trick the drider into handing over the Moonlantern, but removing or exposing it might cure or catastrophically worsen the curse; routine telepathic checks can also reveal a tadpole and prompt orders to report to Disciple Z’rell. Either way, the scene is very likely to end in combat once the Harpers spring the ambush or the drider and guards grow suspicious.
